title: test(ingest-rules): differential fuzzer for the gateway and TS engines

summaries.body:
## Maple review 🔴 **Confidence 4/10** · risky as written Held at 4 because a critical finding is open. 1 critical −3 · tests covered · risk medium A differential fuzzer and property suites for the ingest-rule engines, plus the seven parity bugs it found: byte-based scan cap, Rust's Unicode shorthands, top-level-only protected keys, and regex weight/ambiguity guards. Merge once the new tokenizer stops hanging on an unclosed `\p{`. - `portableRegexSource` rewrites `\d \w \s \b .` to the `regex` crate's meaning - `scanCut` counts UTF-8 bytes and cuts on a character boundary in the TS engine - Protected keys are skipped only at the top level, in Rust and TS alike - `regexProblem` refuses ambiguous repetitions and over-weight patterns at save time ### Before merge - [ ] **Manual** · Re-save stored ingest rules the new checks reject (`a*a*b`, `[\W]`): the TS engine skips them while the gateway still applies them ### Findings
🔴 Critical · F1 · regexProblem never returns for \p{ or \u{ with no closing brace correctness · [`packages/domain/src/ingest-rules.ts:345`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/3ef20c2ae1a72a3ea299364e3176ef6df3284582/packages/domain/src/ingest-rules.ts#L345) `atomEnd` returns `source.indexOf("}", at) + 1`, which is `0` when the brace is missing, so `hasRepeatedVariableGroup` (ingest-rules.ts:213) sets `at = 0` and its `while (at < pattern.length)` loop (line 210) spins forever. `portableRegexSource` lets `\p{` through (it pushes the rest of the source at line 288), so `regexProblem("\\p{")` hangs instead of reaching the "not a valid regular expression" message at line 508 — freezing the rule editor and hanging `IngestRuleService` (`packages/backend/src/services/org/IngestRuleService.ts:114`) on save. ``` if ("pPux".includes(kind) && source[at + 2] === "{") { const close = source.indexOf("}", at) return close === -1 ? at + 2 : close + 1 } ```
### Production impact
Production traffic of the changed files (last 7 days) | File | Calls/day | Busiest operations | | --- | ---: | --- | | `packages/ingest-rules/src/fuzz-arbitraries.ts` | 4.6k | `GET /health` 2.6k/day, 0.0% err
`GET` 1.0k/day, 1.5% err
`GET` 617/day, 12.7% err |
What was checked - Rust `redact_entry(kv, top_level)` matches the TS `redactMap`: top-level `maple_org_id` untouched, nested `user.service.name` redacted in the new fixture - `SHORTHANDS`/`BOUNDARY` (ingest-rules.ts:253-270) reproduce the `regex` crate's Unicode `\w \d \s \b`, with `\p{M}`-style classes - The UTF-8 scan cap is pinned by the `scanCut` property in engine.test.ts rather than a constant

inline.body:
> [!CAUTION]
> **`regexProblem` never returns for `\p{` or `\u{` with no closing brace**
>
> <sub>F1 · Critical · correctness</sub>

`atomEnd` returns `source.indexOf("}", at) + 1`, which is `0` when the brace is missing, so `hasRepeatedVariableGroup` (ingest-rules.ts:213) sets `at = 0` and its `while (at < pattern.length)` loop (line 210) spins forever. `portableRegexSource` lets `\p{` through (it pushes the rest of the source at line 288), so `regexProblem("\\p{")` hangs instead of reaching the "not a valid regular expression" message at line 508 — freezing the rule editor and hanging `IngestRuleService` (`packages/backend/src/services/org/IngestRuleService.ts:114`) on save.

```
Never let `atomEnd` return a position at or below `at`: fall back to `at + 2` when the brace is unclosed. A `regexProblem` case for `"\\p{"` and `"\\u{"` would keep it from regressing.
```

```suggestion
		if ("pPux".includes(kind) && source[at + 2] === "{") {
			const close = source.indexOf("}", at)
			return close === -1 ? at + 2 : close + 1
		}
```

> [!WARNING]
> **`\^+`, `\$+` are rejected though both engines accept them**
>
> <sub>F2 · Warning · correctness</sub>

The `^`/`$` half of the probe has no `(?<!\\)` guard (the `\b` half has one), so an escaped literal caret or dollar followed by a quantifier — `\$+`, `\^+`, `\$*`, `\^{2}`, `\${2}` — is refused with "\\b, \\B, ^ and $ cannot be repeated". Those are ordinary literal repetitions that compile and match in linear time in both the `regex` crate and JS, so a customer cannot save such a pattern. Add `\\` to the lookbehind's class; `[*+?{]` on an unescaped `^`/`$` is still caught, and `[^a]+` stays unaffected.

```suggestion
	[/(?<!\\)\\[bB][*+?{]|(?<![\\[])[\^$][*+?{]/u, "\\b, \\B, ^ and $ cannot be repeated"],
```

> [!WARNING]
> **`^` and `$` inside a character class are literals but are rejected as repeated assertions**
>
> <sub>F3 · Warning · correctness</sub>

The `(?<![\\[])[\^$][*+?{]` half of the probe only skips a `^`/`$` that directly follows `[`, so a literal one deeper in a class is refused with "\b, \B, ^ and $ cannot be repeated". `[#$*]` and `[a-zA-Z0-9$*!]+` both hit the probe at this head and cannot be saved, though both engines accept them and neither repeats an assertion.

```
Probe the pattern with character classes blanked out (`pattern.replace(/\[(?:\\.|[^\\\]])*\]/gu, "")`) instead of the raw text, so the lookbehind on `[` is unnecessary and class-interior literals are skipped.
```
